prototype.mode_head: TF-IDF command unigrams/bigrams + balanced logistic regression
prototype.association_head: balanced pairwise logistic ranker on command cosine and ordered action-bigram cosine; predicted mode probabilities enter as additive and interaction features
prototype.training_pairs: task-balanced; positives share benchmark/task_id; negatives are different task IDs within the same benchmark; human-human, human-agent, and cross-source Agent-Agent represented when available
prototype.evaluation: 5 outer GroupKFold folds by task; training mode features are inner-group out-of-fold; candidate retrieval restricted to same benchmark
prototype.score_semantics: ranking score trained on balanced sampled pairs; not prevalence-calibrated probability and not same-campaign probability
prototype.oracle: oracle_mode_upper_bound uses true human/agent labels at prediction and is diagnostic only, not deployable
prototype.script_class: unsupported: no public script-labeled traces in the selected data

audit.task_split: all traces for one benchmark/task_id remain in a single outer fold

mode_head.interpretation: expert terminal-session versus selected Agent tool-call records; label is confounded by capture modality

limitations: The target is the same CTF challenge ID, not the same attack activity, campaign, or APT actor.
Human terminal transcripts and Agent tool-call records have different collection modalities; execution-mode predictions may learn this confound.
No script-labeled traces are available, so the prototype cannot distinguish fixed scripts from people or Agents.
Pair scores are ranking scores under balanced pair sampling; real-world prevalence calibration and decision thresholds are untested.
Only 40 independent task groups across three selected benchmarks are available; intervals are exploratory.
The oracle mode result uses ground-truth labels and is not a usable detector; it bounds diagnostic potential only.
